# watchpoint_api_key (Resource)

A tenant API key. The plaintext secret is returned only at creation and on rotation, so it is written to Terraform state and must be treated as a secret. `name`, `scopes` and `expires_in_days` cannot be changed in place and replace the key; `enabled` and `rotate_trigger` are applied without replacement. The provider credential needs BOTH `apikeys.manage` (to create, rotate, pause and revoke) and `settings.manage` (to list, which is how this resource reads state). A token holding only `apikeys.manage` will create a key successfully and then fail on the next refresh.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A scoped, non-expiring key for a CI pipeline that only needs to read monitors
# and push deployment markers.
resource "watchpoint_api_key" "ci" {
  name   = "ci-pipeline"
  scopes = ["monitors.read", "deployments.write"]
}

# A key that expires, is rotated on a schedule, and starts paused until someone
# is ready to cut over to it.
resource "watchpoint_api_key" "integration" {
  name            = "partner-integration"
  scopes          = ["monitors.read", "alerts.read"]
  expires_in_days = 90
  enabled         = false

  # Change this value to issue a new secret in place. The key keeps its id, name
  # and scopes, and the previous secret stops working immediately.
  rotate_trigger = "2026-q1"
}

# A full-access key. Prefer an explicit scope list over the wildcard wherever the
# consumer's needs are known.
resource "watchpoint_api_key" "admin" {
  name   = "break-glass"
  scopes = ["*"]
}

# The secret exists only in state and in this output. Mark any output that
# carries it as sensitive, and treat the state file as a secret store.
output "ci_api_key" {
  value     = watchpoint_api_key.ci.api_key
  sensitive = true
}

# The prefix is safe to log, display, or use to identify a key in the portal.
output "ci_api_key_prefix" {
  value = watchpoint_api_key.ci.key_prefix
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Human-readable name shown in the portal and on the audit trail.
- `scopes` (Set of String) Scopes granted to the key, for example `monitors.read`. Required: the API no longer defaults a blank list to full access. Use `["*"]` only for a key that truly needs everything, or `["scim"]` for an IdP provisioning key. Unknown scopes are rejected by the API against its scope catalog.

### Optional

- `allowed_ip_ranges` (Set of String) Per-key IPv4/IPv6 CIDR allowlist, applied on top of the tenant allowlist. A request from any other address is refused with `403 ip_not_allowed`. Fixed at creation, so changing it replaces the key.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the key is currently usable. Setting this to `false` pauses the key without revoking it, so it can be resumed later with the same secret. Defaults to `true`.
- `expires_in_days` (Number) Lifetime in days from creation. Omit for a key that never expires. This is a create-time input; the resulting timestamp is exported as `expires_at`.
- `rotate_trigger` (String) Arbitrary value that rotates the secret when it changes. Change it (for example to a new date) to issue a fresh `api_key` in place, keeping the same `id`, name and scopes. Rotation invalidates the previous secret immediately.
- `service_account_id` (String) Mint the key for a `watchpoint_service_account` instead of the calling user. The key is then capped by the account's role whatever its scopes say, and stops working when the account is deactivated or deleted.

### Read-Only

- `api_key` (String, Sensitive) The plaintext API key. Returned only at creation and on rotation, so it is stored in state and anyone with state access can read it. It is **not** recoverable by `terraform import`: an imported key has a null `api_key` until it is rotated.
- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp (RFC 3339).
- `expires_at` (String) Expiry timestamp (RFC 3339), or null when the key does not expire.
- `id` (String) API key ID.
- `key_prefix` (String) Truncated, non-secret prefix of the key, safe to log or display.
- `last_used_at` (String) Timestamp of the last authenticated request made with this key, or null when it has never been used.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import restores every attribute except api_key, which the API returns only once
# at creation and can never return again. Rotate the key after importing if the
# configuration needs the secret in state.
terraform import watchpoint_api_key.example apikey_001
```
